definition.given: Account cleanup shows a small workspace containing one 13,858-byte JPEG and an empty workspace containing no photos. Both are cleanup candidates that may be suspended.
definition.when: The administrator sets Max photos and Max storage (MB) to 1 and compares the candidates' Content values before deciding which workspaces to suspend.
definition.observed: The Content column shows small workspace as "1 photo" and "0.0 MB", while empty workspace shows "0 photos" and the same "0.0 MB" storage value.
definition.require: Content must clearly distinguish empty workspaces from those with small nonzero storage amounts before the administrator decides which workspaces to suspend.
allow: Small nonzero amounts may be shown using suitable units, additional decimal precision, or accessible exact-value details.
Photo counts may accompany the storage values.

theory.title: Datatips and exact values
theory.reference: Designing Interfaces, Third Edition, Chapter 9: Showing Complex Data; designing-interfaces/chapters/ch09-complex-data.md
theory.rationale: The cleanup table supports comparison and selection. Showing different storage amounts as 0.0 MB hides a distinction needed for the decision. The interface should provide sufficient precision directly or through accessible details.

theory.title: Preview and action safety net
theory.reference: Designing Interfaces, Third Edition, Chapter 8: Actions and Commands; designing-interfaces/chapters/ch08-actions.md
theory.rationale: Suspending a workspace affects access and may lead to deletion. Administrators need to identify workspaces containing data before submitting their selection, so the preview must represent storage amounts accurately.

reference_observation: Content shows "0 B" for the empty workspace and "14 KB" for the small workspace.
requirement_rationale: Administrators use storage amounts to decide which workspaces to clean up. Distinguishing empty workspaces from those containing data helps them make an informed decision.
